conventions.convention: The raw moments are μC=[B1,B2]+IJ and μR=[B1,B1†]+[B2,B2†]+II†−J†J. Regularity requires both the word-span stability condition and the invariant-kernel costability condition. The zero-level quotient is by U(V).
Donaldson's displayed source real equation has −PP†+Q†Q, whereas the raw real moment has +II†−J†J. Entrywise conjugation is not asserted to identify these conventions.
S4 has the unit round metric and positive stereographic orientation dx0∧dx1∧dx2∧dx3, with z1=x0+ix1 and z2=x2+ix3. ASD means F+=(F+*F)/2=0.
Curvature is anti-Hermitian, qN=−(8π²)⁻¹∫trN(F∧F), and the charge-k ASD sector has qN=−k. The determinant Chern-form convention is det(I−F/(2πi)).
The real structure sends (λ1,λ2,μ1,μ2) to (−conj(λ2),conj(λ1),−conj(μ2),conj(μ1)). Finite real lines satisfy μ1=z1λ1−conj(z2)λ2 and μ2=z2λ1+conj(z1)λ2; infinity is λ1=λ2=0.

The Ward metric is induced by the holomorphic reality pairing: hx(s,t)=bz(s(z),t(σz)), linear in s and conjugate-linear in t. Positivity is required on every real-line section space; metric parallelness is a conclusion.
The compact torus acts on raw data by (t1B1,t2B2,Ih⁻¹,t1t2hJ), with h=diag(eα⁻¹), and on ASD objects by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing by h.
The first-order clause uses D=C[ε]/(ε²), with ε†=ε, regular reduction, the stated locally-free and cohomology-base-change conditions, and only reduction and ε↦rε for real r.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated AC and projective GAGA hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between the specified framed ASD classes and framed positive Hermitian Ward bundles trivial on every real twistor line, preserving charge and the specified compact torus actions.

For complex-moment-zero raw data, DD† has diagonal blocks b†b and a†a and off-diagonal blocks μC and μC†, with b†b−a†a=μR. At zero moments, regularity is equivalent to D being onto at every finite point; the resulting projection connection is ASD. The displayed homogeneous maps give a bundle monad trivial on every real line, with framing W at infinity.

Under its exact coupled-vanishing, projective-family and Chern-character inputs, the Ward bundle has the two stated H1(−2) vanishings and a canonical three-term Beilinson monad with coefficient dimensions k, 2k+N, k. Flat parallel summands are retained.

The specified positive Ward monad of dimensions k,2k+N,k has the raw zero-moment normal form, with regularity, residual U(k) action, projection connection equal to the Ward connection, smooth extension and framing at infinity, and k=−qN=c2(E)[S4].
For the specified framed unitary ASD bundle on round S4, the determinant connection is flat, its framing determines a unique global unit parallel section, and qN=−c2(E)[S4] is a nonpositive integer.

Under its stated conditional supplier hypotheses, the construction gives a T-equivariant bijection between regular zero-moment ADHM data modulo U(V) and the specified framed ASD charge-k sector, with N≥2 and k≥0. Its first-order assertion is restricted to the displayed family range.

concerns.concern: The final Statement asserts that, within its dual-number range, the correspondence is compatible with first-order framed deformations and identifies their tangent spaces. Proof 5.1 obtains this by composing [A2]–[A5], but [A4], thm-qftx-framed-penrose-ward-correspondence-on-s4, states and proves a correspondence for ordinary complex bundles and smooth connections, without a dual-number family or infinitesimal gauge-equivalence clause. The normal-form supplier supplies first-order monad extraction, and the P2 supplier supplies first-order sheaf correspondence; neither supplies the missing Ward-family equivalence. The ASD-side first-order objects and tangent quotient are also not explicitly defined here. The ordinary bijection does not by itself establish this additional conclusion. An exact first-order Ward argument, including its inverse and based gauges, remains to be supplied or explicitly assumed.

The Statement places H and ch in singular cohomology, but Facts F1/F4 cite def-chern-character-and-todd-class, whose Definition constructs the algebraic Chern character in the rational Chow ring of a smooth scheme. The cited Chern–Weil comparison concerns differential forms and topological classes, not the Chow-to-singular comparison. The numerical calculation is sound after an elementary additional justification: split the finite monad sequences smoothly and compute the topological Chern character of the resulting sums of line bundles. That domain transition is currently left implicit.

alerts.finding: The sources metadata attributes 'The ADHM construction of Yang–Mills instantons' at https://arxiv.org/pdf/2205.08639 to 'Andrew J. Donaldson'. The opened paper's title page identifies its author as Simon Donaldson; the assigned batch consistently uses Simon K. Donaldson. This is an attribution error.

seams_checked.note: The raw signs, stability/costability, zero-level regular quotient, positive-FI stable quotient and P2 locally-free boundary match the opened suppliers. The first-order P2 range is retained.
ASD is F+=0 and q uses the negative trace. The batch proves its U(N) determinant and charge extension locally rather than promoting the supplier's special SU(2) integrality clause.
The opened Cartan–Bianchi supplier uses the same right-action connection and curvature conventions. Taking trace removes the commutator and gives the closed determinant curvature used here.

The consumers apply the supplied two H1(−2) vanishings to precisely the vertical/horizontal Ward Dolbeault operator, with the same incidence and orientation. They explicitly avoid inferring transform-map existence from a vanishing-only Statement.

The intrinsic raw normal form, positive pairing, U(k) residual action, compact chain factors and restricted dual-number base-change range are faithfully retained. This supplier does not itself establish the ASD-side first-order Ward bridge identified in concerns.
The positive-FI scalar witness uses the supplier's exact P2 maps and explicitly computes the ideal sheaf. The zero-dimensional datum satisfies the supplied regularity conditions vacuously.
The charge-zero example applies the action identity in the ASD sector with B=−trN, obtaining flatness without claiming general U(N) integrality from the SU(2) clause.

The opened instanton-count consumer preserves qN=−k, the regular zero-FI restriction, conditional analytic prerequisites, rank-one boundary and stated first-order qualifications. It expressly makes no ordinary-ASD fixed-point-series claim. Its citation is faithful even though the supplier's first-order proof remains a concern.
